items.title: California passes law to ban ultra-processed foods from school lunches
items.raw_content: What you need to know: Governor Gavin Newsom today signed AB 1264, a first-in-the-nation law phasing out the most concerning ultra-processed foods from California schools. LOS ANGELES – Building on California’s long-standing leadership to protect children’s health and set higher nutrition standards — from his signature on laws banning dangerous food dyes and chemicals to implementing universal school meals — Governor Gavin Newsom today signed AB 1264 by Assemblymember Jesse Gabriel (D-San Fernando Valley), a bipartisan, first-in-the-nation law providing a statutory definition of ultra-processed foods (UPF). This landmark law will phase out the most concerning ultra-processed foods from school meals in California.
items.title_zh: 加州通过法律，禁止学校午餐提供超加工食品
items.summary: Governor Gavin Newsom signed AB 1264, a bipartisan first-in-the-nation law that defines ultra-processed foods and phases the most concerning ones out of California school meals.

items.title: Figure 03, our 3rd generation humanoid robot
items.raw_content: Today we’re introducing Figure 03, our 3rd generation humanoid robot. Figure 03 is designed for Helix, the home, and the world at scale. Our goal is to deliver a truly general-purpose robot - one that can perform human-like tasks and learn directly from people. To realize this vision, our engineering and design teams completed a ground-up hardware and software redesign to ship Figure 03 for: Helix: Figure 03 features a completely redesigned sensory suite and hand system which is purpose-built to enable Helix - Figure's proprietary vision-language-action AI.

items.title: Why is everything so scalable?
items.raw_content: I’m entirely convinced that basically every developer alive today heard the adage “dress for the job you want, not the job you have” and figured that, since they always wear jeans and a t-shirt anyway, they might as well apply it to their systems’ architecture. This explains why the stack of every single company I’ve seen is invariably AWS/GCP with at least thirty microservices (how else will you keep the code tidy?), a distributed datastore that charges per query but whose reads depend on how long it’s been before the last write, a convoluted orchestrator to make sure that you never know which actual computer your code runs on, autoscaling so random midnight breakages ensure you don’t get too complacent with your sleep schedule, and exactly two customers (well, potential customers). I don’t know the exact point when everything went wrong, but I suspect it was somewhere in the 2000s, whe
items.title_zh: 为什么一切都要“可扩展”？
items.summary: A satirical post argues that many companies over-engineer their systems with cloud platforms, dozens of microservices, distributed datastores, orchestrators and autoscaling, in some cases for only a couple of potential customers.

items.title: Subway Builder: A realistic subway simulation game
items.raw_content: Subway Builder is a hyperrealistic transit simulation game. Build a new subway system from the ground up while dealing with real-world constraints and costs. Millions of commuters are generated from Census and Redistricter data and simulated using the same pathfinding algorithms you use on your phone. Your job is to design a route network that gets the most people to their destination as fast as possible. Juggle station placement, transfer dynamics, and train frequency to maximize ridership.

items.summary: Subway Builder is a hyperrealistic transit simulation game in which players build a subway system from the ground up under real-world constraints and costs. items.title: Examples are the best documentation
items.raw_content: When I'm searching for docs, 95% of the time a single example would suffice. Yet, 95% of the time I can't find one in any official source. It seems that by default formal technical documentation is targeted towards someone who's deeply immersed in the ecosystem. But many developers have to juggle a lot of "worlds" in their heads daily. When jumping between projects, languages and frameworks, it takes a considerable amount of mental energy to restore the context and understand what is going on.
items.title_zh: 示例就是最好的文档
items.summary: A blog post argues that a single example would usually suffice when searching documentation, yet official sources rarely offer one. The author says developers juggling many projects, languages and frameworks spend considerable mental energy restoring context.
